CURRENT_DATE().description:
CURRENT_DATE([time_zone: STRING]) → DATE
Returns today's date, in the given time zone or UTC.

DATE().description:
DATE(timestamp_expr: TIMESTAMP[, time_zone: STRING]) → DATE
Makes a DATE from its parts, or takes the date of a TIMESTAMP or DATETIME.

DATE_ADD().description:
DATE_ADD(date_expr: DATE, interval: INTERVAL) → DATE
Adds a number of days, weeks, months, quarters or years to a date.

DATE_SUB().description:
DATE_SUB(date_expr: DATE, interval: INTERVAL) → DATE
Subtracts a number of days, weeks, months, quarters or years from a date.

DATE_DIFF().description:
DATE_DIFF(end_date: DATE, start_date: DATE, granularity: date part) → INT64
Returns the number of `granularity` boundaries between two dates: `end_date` minus `start_date`.

DATE_TRUNC().description:
DATE_TRUNC(date_value: DATE | DATETIME, granularity: date part) → same type as the value
Truncates a date to the start of the given granularity.

FORMAT_DATE().description:
FORMAT_DATE(format_string: STRING, date_expr: DATE) → STRING
Formats a date as a string, by format elements.

PARSE_DATE().description:
PARSE_DATE(format_string: STRING, date_string: STRING) → DATE
Reads a DATE from a string, by format elements. The whole string must match the format.

LAST_DAY().description:
LAST_DAY(date_expr: DATE | DATETIME[, date_part: date part]) → DATE
Returns the last day of the month, or of the given period, that holds the date.

EXTRACT().description:
EXTRACT(part: date part FROM value: DATE | DATETIME | TIME | TIMESTAMP [AT TIME ZONE time_zone: STRING]) → INT64 (DATE, DATETIME or TIME for those parts)
Returns one part of a date, datetime, time or timestamp.

GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY().description:
GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY(start_date: DATE, end_date: DATE[, interval: INTERVAL]) → ARRAY<DATE>
Returns an array of dates from `start_date` to `end_date`, both included, a step apart.

CURRENT_DATETIME().description:
CURRENT_DATETIME([time_zone: STRING]) → DATETIME
Returns the date and time now, in the given time zone or UTC, with no time zone kept.

DATETIME().description:
DATETIME(timestamp_expr: TIMESTAMP[, time_zone: STRING]) → DATETIME
Makes a DATETIME from its parts, from a DATE and a TIME, or from a TIMESTAMP in a time zone.

DATETIME_ADD().description:
DATETIME_ADD(datetime_expr: DATETIME, interval: INTERVAL) → DATETIME
Adds an interval to a datetime.

DATETIME_SUB().description:
DATETIME_SUB(datetime_expr: DATETIME, interval: INTERVAL) → DATETIME
Subtracts an interval from a datetime.

DATETIME_DIFF().description:
DATETIME_DIFF(end_datetime: DATETIME, start_datetime: DATETIME, granularity: datetime part) → INT64
Returns the number of `granularity` boundaries between two datetimes: `end_datetime` minus `start_datetime`.

DATETIME_TRUNC().description:
DATETIME_TRUNC(datetime_value: DATETIME, granularity: datetime part) → DATETIME
Truncates a datetime to the start of the given granularity.

FORMAT_DATETIME().description:
FORMAT_DATETIME(format_string: STRING, datetime_expr: DATETIME) → STRING
Formats a datetime as a string, by format elements.

PARSE_DATETIME().description:
PARSE_DATETIME(format_string: STRING, datetime_string: STRING) → DATETIME
Reads a DATETIME from a string, by format elements. The whole string must match the format.

CURRENT_TIMESTAMP().description:
CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() → TIMESTAMP
Returns the time now, as a TIMESTAMP.

TIMESTAMP().description:
TIMESTAMP(value: STRING | DATE | DATETIME[, time_zone: STRING]) → TIMESTAMP
Makes a TIMESTAMP from a string, a date or a datetime, read in the given time zone or UTC.

TIMESTAMP_ADD().description:
TIMESTAMP_ADD(timestamp_expr: TIMESTAMP, interval: INTERVAL) → TIMESTAMP
Adds an interval to a timestamp.

TIMESTAMP_SUB().description:
TIMESTAMP_SUB(timestamp_expr: TIMESTAMP, interval: INTERVAL) → TIMESTAMP
Subtracts an interval from a timestamp.

TIMESTAMP_DIFF().description:
TIMESTAMP_DIFF(end_timestamp: TIMESTAMP, start_timestamp: TIMESTAMP, granularity: timestamp part) → INT64
Returns the number of whole `granularity` intervals between two timestamps: `end_timestamp` minus `start_timestamp`.

TIMESTAMP_TRUNC().description:
TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(timestamp_value: TIMESTAMP, granularity: timestamp part[, time_zone: STRING]) → TIMESTAMP
Truncates a timestamp to the start of the given granularity, in the given time zone or UTC.

FORMAT_TIMESTAMP().description:
FORMAT_TIMESTAMP(format_string: STRING, timestamp_expr: TIMESTAMP[, time_zone: STRING]) → STRING
Formats a timestamp as a string, by format elements, in the given time zone or UTC.

PARSE_TIMESTAMP().description:
PARSE_TIMESTAMP(format_string: STRING, timestamp_string: STRING[, time_zone: STRING]) → TIMESTAMP
Reads a TIMESTAMP from a string, by format elements, in the given time zone or UTC.

UNIX_SECONDS().description:
UNIX_SECONDS(timestamp_expr: TIMESTAMP) → INT64
Returns the number of seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.

UNIX_MILLIS().description:
UNIX_MILLIS(timestamp_expr: TIMESTAMP) → INT64
Returns the number of milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.

TIMESTAMP_SECONDS().description:
TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(seconds: INT64) → TIMESTAMP
Reads a number of seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC as a TIMESTAMP.

TIMESTAMP_MILLIS().description:
TIMESTAMP_MILLIS(milliseconds: INT64) → TIMESTAMP
Reads a number of milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC as a TIMESTAMP.

GENERATE_TIMESTAMP_ARRAY().description:
GENERATE_TIMESTAMP_ARRAY(start_timestamp: TIMESTAMP, end_timestamp: TIMESTAMP, interval: INTERVAL) → ARRAY<TIMESTAMP>
Returns an array of timestamps from `start_timestamp` to `end_timestamp`, both included, an interval apart.

CONCAT().description:
CONCAT(value: STRING | BYTES, value: STRING | BYTES, ...) → STRING | BYTES
Joins values into one. Returns NULL if any value is NULL.

LENGTH().description:
LENGTH(value: STRING | BYTES) → INT64
Returns the length of a value: characters for a STRING, bytes for BYTES.

LOWER().description:
LOWER(value: STRING | BYTES) → STRING | BYTES
Returns the value in lower case.

UPPER().description:
UPPER(value: STRING | BYTES) → STRING | BYTES
Returns the value in upper case.

INITCAP().description:
INITCAP(value: STRING[, delimiters: STRING]) → STRING
Upper-cases the first character of each word and lower-cases the rest.

TRIM().description:
TRIM(value: STRING | BYTES[, set_of_characters_to_remove: STRING | BYTES]) → STRING | BYTES
Removes whitespace, or the given characters, from both ends of a value.

LTRIM().description:
LTRIM(value: STRING | BYTES[, set_of_characters_to_remove: STRING | BYTES]) → STRING | BYTES
Removes whitespace, or the given characters, from the start of a value.

RTRIM().description:
RTRIM(value: STRING | BYTES[, set_of_characters_to_remove: STRING | BYTES]) → STRING | BYTES
Removes whitespace, or the given characters, from the end of a value.

SUBSTR().description:
SUBSTR(value: STRING | BYTES, position: INT64[, length: INT64]) → STRING | BYTES
Returns the part of a value that starts at `position` and is `length` long.

REPLACE().description:
REPLACE(original_value: STRING | BYTES, from_pattern: STRING | BYTES, to_pattern: STRING | BYTES) → STRING | BYTES
Replaces every occurrence of `from_pattern` with `to_pattern`. Matches exact text, not a regular expression.

SPLIT().description:
SPLIT(value: STRING | BYTES[, delimiter: STRING | BYTES]) → ARRAY<STRING> | ARRAY<BYTES>
Splits a value at each delimiter into an array.

STARTS_WITH().description:
STARTS_WITH(value: STRING | BYTES, prefix: STRING | BYTES) → BOOL
Whether a value starts with `prefix`.

ENDS_WITH().description:
ENDS_WITH(value: STRING | BYTES, suffix: STRING | BYTES) → BOOL
Whether a value ends with `suffix`.

CONTAINS_SUBSTR().description:
CONTAINS_SUBSTR(expression: ANY, search_value: STRING) → BOOL
Whether `search_value` is in `expression`, ignoring case. The expression can also be a STRUCT, an ARRAY or JSON, searched in every field.

STRPOS().description:
STRPOS(value: STRING | BYTES, subvalue: STRING | BYTES) → INT64
Returns the 1-based position of the first `subvalue` in `value`, or 0 if it is not found.

INSTR().description:
INSTR(source_value: STRING | BYTES, search_value: STRING | BYTES[, position: INT64][, occurrence: INT64]) → INT64
Returns the 1-based position of an occurrence of `search_value`, or 0 if it is not found.

LPAD().description:
LPAD(original_value: STRING | BYTES, return_length: INT64[, pattern: STRING | BYTES]) → STRING | BYTES
Pads the start of a value with `pattern` until it is `return_length` long.

RPAD().description:
RPAD(original_value: STRING | BYTES, return_length: INT64[, pattern: STRING | BYTES]) → STRING | BYTES
Pads the end of a value with `pattern` until it is `return_length` long.

LEFT().description:
LEFT(value: STRING | BYTES, length: INT64) → STRING | BYTES
Returns the first `length` characters, or bytes, of a value.

RIGHT().description:
RIGHT(value: STRING | BYTES, length: INT64) → STRING | BYTES
Returns the last `length` characters, or bytes, of a value.

REPEAT().description:
REPEAT(original_value: STRING | BYTES, repetitions: INT64) → STRING | BYTES
Returns a value repeated a number of times.

REVERSE().description:
REVERSE(value: STRING | BYTES) → STRING | BYTES
Returns a value with its characters, or bytes, in reverse order.

FORMAT().description:
FORMAT(format_string: STRING, value: ANY, ...) → STRING
Formats values into a string, printf style: `%s` a string, `%d` an integer, `%f` a float, `%t` any value as text.

REGEXP_CONTAINS().description:
REGEXP_CONTAINS(value: STRING | BYTES, regexp: STRING) → BOOL
Whether `value` has a match of the regular expression anywhere in it.

REGEXP_EXTRACT().description:
REGEXP_EXTRACT(value: STRING | BYTES, regexp: STRING[, position: INT64][, occurrence: INT64]) → STRING | BYTES
Returns the first part of `value` that matches the regular expression, or NULL. With a capturing group, returns what the group matched.

REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL().description:
REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL(value: STRING | BYTES, regexp: STRING) → ARRAY<STRING> | ARRAY<BYTES>
Returns every part of `value` that matches the regular expression.

REGEXP_REPLACE().description:
REGEXP_REPLACE(value: STRING | BYTES, regexp: STRING, replacement: STRING | BYTES) → STRING | BYTES
Replaces every match of the regular expression. In `replacement`, `\1` is what the first group matched.

COUNT().description:
COUNT(expression: ANY) → INT64
Counts the rows, or the rows where the expression is not NULL.

COUNTIF().description:
COUNTIF(condition: BOOL) → INT64
Counts the rows where the condition is TRUE.

SUM().description:
SUM(expression: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64 | INTERVAL) → INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64 | INTERVAL
Returns the sum of the values that are not NULL, or NULL if there are none.

AVG().description:
AVG(expression: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64 | INTERVAL) → FLOAT64 (NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC for those)
Returns the average of the values that are not NULL.

MIN().description:
MIN(expression: any orderable type) → same type as the expression
Returns the smallest value that is not NULL.

MAX().description:
MAX(expression: any orderable type) → same type as the expression
Returns the largest value that is not NULL.

MAX_BY().description:
MAX_BY(x: ANY, y: any orderable type) → same type as x
Returns the value of `x` on the row where `y` is largest.

MIN_BY().description:
MIN_BY(x: ANY, y: any orderable type) → same type as x
Returns the value of `x` on the row where `y` is smallest.

ANY_VALUE().description:
ANY_VALUE(expression: ANY) → same type as the expression
Returns the expression for some row of the group, chosen by BigQuery. NULL only if every row has NULL.

ARRAY_AGG().description:
ARRAY_AGG(expression: any type but ARRAY) → ARRAY
Collects the values of a group into an array.

STRING_AGG().description:
STRING_AGG(expression: STRING | BYTES[, delimiter: STRING | BYTES]) → STRING | BYTES
Joins the values of a group into one string.

LOGICAL_AND().description:
LOGICAL_AND(condition: BOOL) → BOOL
Whether the condition is TRUE for every row where it is not NULL.

LOGICAL_OR().description:
LOGICAL_OR(condition: BOOL) → BOOL
Whether the condition is TRUE for at least one row.

APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT().description:
APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(expression: ANY) → INT64
Estimates the number of different values: faster and cheaper than COUNT(DISTINCT ...) on many rows.

APPROX_QUANTILES().description:
APPROX_QUANTILES(expression: any orderable type, number: INT64) → ARRAY
Estimates the boundaries of `number` equal groups of the values: `number + 1` values, from the minimum to the maximum.

ROW_NUMBER().description:
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...) → INT64
Numbers the rows of each partition 1, 2, 3, ... in the order of ORDER BY, with no ties.

RANK().description:
RANK() OVER (...) → INT64
Ranks the rows of each partition; ties get the same rank and leave a gap (1, 1, 3).

DENSE_RANK().description:
DENSE_RANK() OVER (...) → INT64
Ranks the rows of each partition; ties get the same rank and leave no gap (1, 1, 2).

PERCENT_RANK().description:
PERCENT_RANK() OVER (...) → FLOAT64
Returns the rank of the row in its partition as a fraction from 0 to 1.

NTILE().description:
NTILE(n: INT64) OVER (...) → INT64
Splits the rows of each partition into `n` buckets as equal as can be, and returns the bucket of the row, from 1.

LAG().description:
LAG(value: ANY[, offset: INT64][, default: same type as value]) OVER (...) → same type as the value
Returns the value from a row before the current one in the partition.

LEAD().description:
LEAD(value: ANY[, offset: INT64][, default: same type as value]) OVER (...) → same type as the value
Returns the value from a row after the current one in the partition.

FIRST_VALUE().description:
FIRST_VALUE(value: ANY) OVER (...) → same type as the value
Returns the value on the first row of the window frame.

LAST_VALUE().description:
LAST_VALUE(value: ANY) OVER (...) → same type as the value
Returns the value on the last row of the window frame.

NTH_VALUE().description:
NTH_VALUE(value: ANY, n: INT64) OVER (...) → same type as the value
Returns the value on the `n`th row of the window frame, from 1.

PERCENTILE_CONT().description:
PERCENTILE_CONT(value: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64, percentile: FLOAT64) OVER (...) → FLOAT64 (NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC for those)
Returns the given percentile of the values in the partition, interpolating between rows.

IF().description:
IF(condition: BOOL, true_result: ANY, else_result: ANY) → the type of the results
Returns `true_result` if the condition is TRUE, else `else_result`.

IFNULL().description:
IFNULL(expr: ANY, null_result: ANY) → the type of the arguments
Returns `expr`, or `null_result` when `expr` is NULL.

COALESCE().description:
COALESCE(expr: ANY, expr: ANY, ...) → the type of the arguments
Returns the first argument that is not NULL.

NULLIF().description:
NULLIF(expr: ANY, expr_to_match: ANY) → the type of expr
Returns NULL if `expr` equals `expr_to_match`, else `expr`.

CAST().description:
CAST(expression: ANY AS type: type name [FORMAT format: STRING]) → the type named
Converts a value to another type. Fails the query when it cannot; SAFE_CAST returns NULL instead.

SAFE_CAST().description:
SAFE_CAST(expression: ANY AS type: type name [FORMAT format: STRING]) → the type named
Converts a value to another type, or returns NULL when it cannot.

JSON_VALUE().description:
JSON_VALUE(json_expr: STRING | JSON[, json_path: STRING]) → STRING
Returns the scalar value at a JSON path as a STRING, without quotes. NULL for an object or an array.

JSON_QUERY().description:
JSON_QUERY(json_expr: STRING | JSON, json_path: STRING) → STRING | JSON
Returns the JSON value at a JSON path: an object, an array or a scalar, as JSON text.

JSON_EXTRACT().description:
JSON_EXTRACT(json_expr: STRING | JSON, json_path: STRING) → STRING | JSON
Returns the JSON value at a JSON path. JSON_QUERY is its newer name.

JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR().description:
JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(json_expr: STRING | JSON[, json_path: STRING]) → STRING
Returns the scalar value at a JSON path as a STRING. JSON_VALUE is its newer name.

JSON_QUERY_ARRAY().description:
JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(json_expr: STRING | JSON[, json_path: STRING]) → ARRAY<STRING> | ARRAY<JSON>
Returns the JSON array at a JSON path as an ARRAY of its elements.

JSON_VALUE_ARRAY().description:
JSON_VALUE_ARRAY(json_expr: STRING | JSON[, json_path: STRING]) → ARRAY<STRING>
Returns the JSON array of scalars at a JSON path as an ARRAY<STRING>.

PARSE_JSON().description:
PARSE_JSON(json_string: STRING) → JSON
Reads a JSON string as a JSON value.

TO_JSON_STRING().description:
TO_JSON_STRING(value: ANY[, pretty_print: BOOL]) → STRING
Returns any value as JSON text.

ARRAY_LENGTH().description:
ARRAY_LENGTH(array_expr: ARRAY) → INT64
Returns the number of elements of an array, or NULL for a NULL array.

ARRAY_TO_STRING().description:
ARRAY_TO_STRING(array_expr: ARRAY<STRING> | ARRAY<BYTES>, delimiter: STRING | BYTES[, null_text: STRING | BYTES]) → STRING | BYTES
Joins the elements of an array of strings with a delimiter.

ARRAY_CONCAT().description:
ARRAY_CONCAT(array_expr: ARRAY, array_expr: ARRAY, ...) → ARRAY
Joins arrays of the same element type into one.

ARRAY_REVERSE().description:
ARRAY_REVERSE(array_expr: ARRAY) → ARRAY
Returns the array with its elements in reverse order.

GENERATE_ARRAY().description:
GENERATE_ARRAY(start: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64, end: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64[, step: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64]) → ARRAY
Returns an array of numbers from `start` to `end`, both included, `step` apart.

SAFE_DIVIDE().description:
SAFE_DIVIDE(X: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64, Y: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64) → FLOAT64 (NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC for those)
Divides `X` by `Y`, like `X / Y`, but returns NULL instead of failing when `Y` is 0.

ROUND().description:
ROUND(X: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64[, N: INT64][, rounding_mode: STRING]) → FLOAT64 (NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC for those)
Rounds `X` to `N` decimal places; halfway cases round away from zero.

TRUNC().description:
TRUNC(X: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64[, N: INT64]) → FLOAT64 (NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC for those)
Drops the decimal places of `X` beyond `N`, rounding toward zero.

ABS().description:
ABS(X: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64) → same type as X
Returns the absolute value of `X`.

CEIL().description:
CEIL(X: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64) → FLOAT64 (NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC for those)
Returns the smallest whole number not less than `X`.

FLOOR().description:
FLOOR(X: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64) → FLOAT64 (NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC for those)
Returns the largest whole number not greater than `X`.

MOD().description:
MOD(X: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC, Y: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC) → INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC
Returns the remainder of `X` divided by `Y`, with the sign of `X`.

DIV().description:
DIV(X: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC, Y: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC) → INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC
Divides `X` by `Y` and returns the whole part, rounding toward zero.

POW().description:
POW(X: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64, Y: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64) → FLOAT64 (NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC for those)
Returns `X` raised to the power `Y`.

SQRT().description:
SQRT(X: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64) → FLOAT64 (NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC for those)
Returns the square root of `X`.

LOG().description:
LOG(X: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64[, Y: INT64 | NUMERIC | BIGNUMERIC | FLOAT64]) → FLOAT64 (NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC for those)
Returns the logarithm of `X` to base `Y`, or the natural logarithm with no `Y`.

GREATEST().description:
GREATEST(X: any orderable type, X: any orderable type, ...) → the type of the arguments
Returns the largest of the arguments; NULL if any of them is NULL.

LEAST().description:
LEAST(X: any orderable type, X: any orderable type, ...) → the type of the arguments
Returns the smallest of the arguments; NULL if any of them is NULL.

RAND().description:
RAND() → FLOAT64
Returns a random number from 0 (included) to 1 (not included).

GENERATE_UUID().description:
GENERATE_UUID() → STRING
Returns a random UUID as a STRING of 36 characters.

FARM_FINGERPRINT().description:
FARM_FINGERPRINT(value: STRING | BYTES) → INT64
Returns a stable INT64 hash of a value, the same on every run.
